summary: Checked all 12 estimates against the complete 14-page paper. Read the entire 89,961-character markdown, including Appendix A and the references; extracted the cited PDF pages with pymupdf and inspected Figures 1 and 2 in memory. All 30 non-null entries in stats (24 arm means/SDs and six p-value bounds) match the PDF and belong to the stated post-test outcome and AI-versus-comparison contrast. The study total of 95 randomized participants and randomized arm counts of 31 AI, 34 human, and 30 control are printed on PDF pp. 1 and 3. Analysis-specific participant counts are not separately printed; the null analyzed counts appropriately avoid deriving counts from degrees of freedom or substituting randomized counts. All 14 supplied quote-matching flags are false positives. Each of the 12 flagged mean/SD sources explicitly combines two separate verbatim excerpts: the AI post-test values in Section 3.1 (acquisition on PDF p. 5; transfer on PDF p. 6) and the standard-deviation sentence in the Figure 2 caption on PDF p. 6. Both excerpts are present on their cited pages. The two transfer-flexibility p-value quotations also match PDF p. 6: the PDF splits the word control with a discretionary hyphen and a line break. Splitting the disclosed excerpts and normalizing whitespace and discretionary hyphens confirms every source quotation; all are within the 40-word limit. The acquisition p bound applies to originality and flexibility versus both comparison arms, and the transfer p bound applies to flexibility versus both comparison arms. Within-arm p-values and omnibus ANOVA statistics have not been misassigned to pairwise contrasts. The requested codebook fields are supported: novelty for originality, flexibility for within-person category variety, fluency for idea count; human_raters for originality and category_count for flexibility/fluency; participant units; more_creative for originality/flexibility and more_ideas for fluency; ai_vs_bau versus quiet rest and ai_vs_active versus human instruction. The immediate post-tests follow the separate instruction phase, supporting after_ai and outcome_with_ai=false with the already-disclosed inference about post-test AI access. Repeated pre/post measurement does not constitute randomized crossover assignment, so within_person=null is correct. The se_basis codes reflect participant-score post hoc comparisons, including the AI-versus-control transfer-originality comparison shown in Figure 2E; no pair-specific uncertainty is reported for the other five comparisons coded not_reported. The supplied paper contains all six outcome-by-task combinations against both comparison arms, giving 12 records; no additional in-scope outcome or contrast was found. Self-reports, neural outcomes, correlations, baseline comparisons, within-arm changes, omnibus tests, and human-versus-control comparisons are appropriately excluded. Figure-only numbers remain untranscribed under extraction Rule 1. The acquisition-flexibility text/figure inconsistency is a paper reporting issue already disclosed in the extraction; the recorded 7.29 and 2.97 faithfully reproduce the printed text. Completeness beyond the supplied paper cannot be established: Appendix A refers to a separate supplement, including Table S2, but the local supplement manifest lists no files. Independent urllib requests to the article DOI and the named ScienceDirect article URL, with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, both failed with WinError 10013. No missing comparator value or additional estimate was guessed from that unavailable material.
